newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air may have to seek merger - report.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air may have to seek merger - report.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc chief executive officer Gordon Bethune said in a newspaper interview published on Wednesday that the company currently is not pursuing a a merger, but expected consolidation in the airline industry could force it to seek a partner.

The consolidation wave could begin as early as next year, when Bethune predicted in comments to the Houston Chronicle that a proposed alliance between British Airways Plc and AMR Corp's American Airlines would get final approval from the U.S. government.
"For us, it bodes ill because it's a formidable consolidation," he said of the proposed alliance. "Even if they placate us with routes and gates and slots, it's still a challenge for us."
The British government already has approved the British Airways-American alliance, but the U.S. has said it would go along with it only if Britain opened its markets fully to U.S. carriers.
Houston-based Continental has been lobbying for permission to fly into London's Heathrow Airport but has yet to receive it.

Bethune did not say if the British Airways-American alliance would immediately send Continental scurrying for a merger partner, but said a general trend toward airline consolidation was inevitable. "From a historical perspective, yes, it's (consolidation) inevitable. Now the timing on it, it could be anybody's guess," Bethune said.

Continental last week said it broke off merger talks with rival carriers that had been reported to include Delta Air Lines Inc. Neither company would comment on the discussions or why they failed, a policy that Bethune continued with the Chronicle.

He said Continental currently has no plans to talk with potential partners. But, he said, "Does that mean that I will never be or we will never be (interested in future discussions)? We never said that...we don't know what the world is going to be like in 10 years or five years."

Bethune also told the Chronicle that Continental was discussing a marketing alliance with Russian airline Aeroflot which would allow Continental jets to fly from Newark, N.J. to Moscow. A similar partnership was being sought in South America, he said.
Continental will begin an alliance with Air France on April 1 allowing it to hook into Air France's global connections. Bethune said he hoped that an Asian carrier would join in the deal.
